house.dashboard.pages.<name>.code.description: HTML and JavaScript code for the page

house.dashboard.pages.<name>.files.description: Files to be symlinked to the http server for this page
house.dashboard.pages.<name>.files.type: attribute set of (absolute path or string)

house.dashboard.pages.<name>.icon.description: Icon for the tab (FontAwesome class, MDI class, or image URL)

house.dashboard.statusCards.description: Configurable status cards for the dashboard

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.chart.description:
Render a sparkline history chart on the card. Requires
the JSON file to contain a history array (see
`historyField`).

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.color.description: Accent colour (hex or CSS colour) used for the card.

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.defau.description:
Text shown in place of the details line when the card
cannot be loaded.

Text shown in place of the main value when the card
cannot be loaded (missing file, unparsable JSON, absent
field).

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.detai.description:
Static details text used when `detailsJsonField` is null.
Prefer `detailsJsonField` + `detailsFormat` for dynamic
values; this option is kept for backwards compatibility.

Format string for the details line. `{value}` is replaced
with the value of `detailsJsonField`.

Optional key in the JSON file whose value is substituted
into `detailsFormat`. When null, the static `details`
string is shown instead (legacy behaviour).

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.enabl.description: Whether to enable this status card.

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.fileP.description:
Absolute path to the JSON file the card reads when
`source = "file"`. Typically under `/var/lib/zigduck/`.

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.forma.description:
Format string for the main value. `{value}` is replaced
with the value of `jsonField`.

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.group.description:
Group name controlling the card's placement on the
dashboard. Cards sharing the same group are rendered
together, ordered alphabetically by group name.

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.histo.description:
Key in the JSON file holding the array of past values
plotted when `chart = true`.

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.icon.description:
Font Awesome class rendered in the card header. Any free
or pro icon class works. See https://fontawesome.com/search

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.jsonF.description:
Key in the JSON file whose value is substituted into
`format` (as `{value}`) to produce the card's main value.

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.on_cl.description:
Actions to run when the card is clicked. Uses the same
action DSL as automations.

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.sourc.description:
Where the card pulls its value from. Currently only
`file` is supported: a JSON file written by an
MQTT-triggered automation.

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.theme.description:
Visual theme applied to the card. One of:
`neon`, `minimal`, `dark`, `glass`, `colorful`.

house.dashboard.statusCards.<name>.title.description:
Text shown as the card's heading. Unicode and emoji are
supported (e.g. `𝑿𝑴𝑹`, `𝑩𝑻𝑪`).

house.devices.description:
Non-Zigbee devices managed by zigduck — NixOS hosts (system health
published to MQTT), ESP32 hardware (watch, speaker, etc.), and any
other HTTP-addressable endpoint. Each entry is keyed by an arbitrary
name that also becomes its MQTT topic suffix (`zigduck/<name>`) and
the key used by `config.house.devices.<name>.ip` references from
automations (e.g. `curl http://${config.house.devices.watch.ip}/api/...`).

A device may publish its own state JSON (usually `/api/sensors`) and
expose `controls` that render as widgets in the dashboard. Each
control change dispatches the configured `actions`, with the new
value available as `$VALUE`, the device IP as `$IP`, and so on.

house.devices.<name>.controls.description:
Define custom controls surfaced as widgets in the GNOME panel detail view.
Each key is a field name present in the state JSON file.

house.devices.<name>.controls.<name>.act.description:
Actions executed when this control changes. The new value is
available as `$VALUE` (and as `{value}` inside non-shell
actions). `$KEY`, `$DEVICE`, `$IP` and `$MQTT_PAYLOAD`
are also set. Leave empty for read-only `sensor` controls.

house.devices.<name>.controls.<name>.des.description: Optional description of this control action.

house.devices.<name>.controls.<name>.ico.description: Material Design icon name representing this state/value.

house.devices.<name>.controls.<name>.typ.description: Widget type rendered in the frontend.

house.devices.<name>.controls.<name>.val.description: List of allowed values, restricting this control action to only send one of these values.

house.devices.<name>.enable.description: Enables this device to be monitored.

house.devices.<name>.icon.description: Material Design icon name representing this device.

house.devices.<name>.room.description: Room where this device is located

house.devices.<name>.stateEndpoint.description:
State JSON endpoint — extension refetches this after every control
action so the frontend reflects the new value immediately
without waiting for the next MQTT publish.

house.https.description: Public HTTPS URLs (or files containing them) for zigduck's web-facing services: the dashboard and the media library.

house.https.dashboard.url.description:
Public HTTPS URL used to access the dashboard.
This url is used for a secure API connection.

Domain does not need to be publicly accessable, as long as the certificate is valid. 

You need a domain name with a valid TLS certificate. 
A free dynamic DNS provider such as DuckDNS can be used if you do not already have a domain.

house.https.dashboard.urlFile.description:
Path to a file containing the public HTTPS URL used to
access the dashboard.
This url is used for a secure API connection.

Domain does not need to be publicly accessable, as long as the certificate is valid. 

You need a domain name with a valid TLS certificate. 
A free dynamic DNS provider such as DuckDNS can be used if you do not already have a domain.

house.https.media.description: HTTPS configuration for the media library.

house.https.media.url.description:
Public HTTPS URL used to access the media library.

The URL must use HTTPS and should point to the web server
that serves `house.media.root`.

This is required by some media clients, such as Android TV,
when accessing external `.m3u` playlists.

Domain does not need to be publicly accessable, as long as the certificate is valid. 

You need a domain name with a valid TLS certificate. 
A free dynamic DNS provider such as DuckDNS can be used if you do not already have a domain.

house.https.media.urlFile.description:
Path to a file containing the public HTTPS URL used to
access the media library.

The URL must use HTTPS and should point to the web server
that serves `house.media.root`.

This is required by some media clients, such as Android TV,
when accessing external `.m3u` playlists.

Domain does not need to be publicly accessable, as long as the certificate is valid. 

You need a domain name with a valid TLS certificate. 
A free dynamic DNS provider such as DuckDNS can be used if you do not already have a domain.

house.media.audiobooks.description:
Directory containing audiobook folders.
Each audiobook should be in its own subdirectory.

house.media.favouritesFile.description:
File path where the playlist for starred media will be written.
This is a Persistent playlist for the users favourite tracks.
It must be writable by the user executing the tv command.
Should be inside a directory exposed by the web server.

house.media.movies.description:
Directory containing movie folders.
Each movie should be in its own subdirectory, e.g.:
  Movies/Some Movie (2020)/movie.mkv

house.media.music.description:
Directory containing music. Can be flat or hierarchical.

For artist/album search (typ = "music"), each artist or album
should be in its own subdirectory.

For song search (typ = "song"), files are searched recursively
by filename with extensions: mp3, flac, m4a, wav.

For jukebox (typ = "jukebox"), all files under this directory
are shuffled and played.

house.media.musicVideos.description:
Directory containing music video folders.
Each music video should be in its own subdirectory.

house.media.otherVideos.description:
Directory containing miscellaneous video files.
Videos are searched recursively by filename with extensions:
  mp4, mkv, avi, mov
No folder structure requirement beyond being under this path.

house.media.playlistFile.description:
File path where the generated playlist will be written.
This file is overwritten each time the TV controller creates a new playlist.
It must be writable by the user executing the tv command.
Should be inside a directory exposed by the web server.

house.media.podcasts.description:
Directory containing podcast folders.
Each podcast should be in its own subdirectory.
Episodes are files inside those folders.

house.media.root.description:
Absolute path to the root media directory.
All other media directories should be subdirectories of this path.
The URL configured at `config.house.https.media.urlFile` should point to this directory as the root of a file server.

house.media.tv.description:
Directory containing TV show folders.
Each show should be in its own subdirectory.
Inside each show folder, seasons are expected in folders like:
  "Season 1", "Season 01", "S01", "s01"
Episode files go inside those season folders.

house.media.youtubePasswordFile.description:
Path to a file containing a YouTube Data API v3 key.
The file should contain only the API key string (no extra whitespace).

To obtain a key:
  1. Go to https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials
  2. Create a new API key.
  4. Save the key to a file.

If set to null, YouTube playback is disabled.

house.rooms.description: A set of rooms in the house with their attributes.

house.rooms.<name>.entertainment.description:
Marks this room as a Philips Hue Play HDMI Sync Box
entertainment area. Rooms with this flag enabled are
eligible for Hue-synced lighting (see
`house.zigbee.hueSyncBox`).

house.rooms.<name>.icon.description:
Material Design Icons (MDI) identifier rendered by the
dashboard for this room. Must include the `mdi:` prefix.
Catalogue: https://pictogrammers.com/library/mdi/

house.tv.description:
Attrset of TV devices, keyed by an arbitrary device name
(e.g. `"livingroom"`). Each entry describes how to reach the TV
over ADB, its room, its channel lineup, and how to map logical
playback/navigation actions to Android keycodes.

house.tv.<name>.apps.description: App package names and activities for this TV device

house.tv.<name>.channels.<name>.cmd.description: Sequence of ADB commands to launch the channel, separated by `&&`. Overrides `stream_url` and `id`.

house.tv.<name>.channels.<name>.icon.description: Optional file path for channel icon used on dashboard frontend

house.tv.<name>.channels.<name>.id.description: Numeric channel ID used when no `cmd` or `stream_url` is provided.

house.tv.<name>.channels.<name>.scrape_u.description: URL used by tv-scraper to fetch TV guide data for this channel.

house.tv.<name>.channels.<name>.scraper.description:
Per-channel scraper overrides, layered on top of the
device-level `scraper` and the scraper's built-in
defaults.

house.tv.<name>.channels.<name>.scraper..description:
Fallback duration when the next entry's start time can't
be parsed.
Scraper default: `30`.

XPath relative to a row, locating the description element.
Set to `""` to disable descriptions.
Scraper default: `.//p`.

Only relevant for 12-hour formats that lack an explicit
AM/PM marker. Once the previous programme reached or
passed this hour, later ambiguous AM hours are promoted
to PM. `null` disables the heuristic.
house.tv.<name>.channels.<name>.scraper..type: null or integer between 0 and 23 (both inclusive)

house.tv.<name>.channels.<name>.scraper..description:
XPath selecting each programme row.
Scraper default: `//table[@id="channel-schedule"]//tr`.

Attribute of the time element to read. Set to `""` to
always use the element's text content.
Scraper default: `"datetime"`.

strptime formats tried in order, after ISO 8601 is
attempted.
Scraper default: `[ "%H:%M" "%H.%M" ]`.

Regex applied to the raw time string before strptime.
Set to `""` to disable stripping — required when the
format keeps a literal AM/PM marker.
Scraper default: `"[^\\d:\\.]"`.

XPath relative to a row, locating the element containing
the start time.
Scraper default: `.//time`.

Fixed offset applied to every parsed time, in hours. May
be fractional (e.g. `5.5`). `null` = use the scraper's
built-in global `TIME_OFFSET`.
house.tv.<name>.channels.<name>.scraper..type: null or signed integer or floating point number

house.tv.<name>.channels.<name>.scraper..description:
XPath relative to a row, locating the title element.
Scraper default: `.//a[contains(@class, "program-title")]`.

house.tv.<name>.channels.<name>.stream_u.description: Direct stream URL to play on the device. Used when `cmd` is empty, overrides `id`.

house.tv.<name>.enable.description:
Whether to enable communication with this TV via ADB.
This requires that network debugging is turned on in the TV's developer options.
It is also strongly recommended to install the VLC Media Player application on the device.

house.tv.<name>.isDefault.description:
Whether this TV is the default device when multiple TVs are defined
and no specific room or IP is requested.

house.tv.<name>.keymap.description: Mapping of logical actions to Android keycodes

house.tv.<name>.keymap.power_off.description: Android Keycode for turning the TV off

house.tv.<name>.keymap.power_on.description: Android Keycode for turning the TV on

house.tv.<name>.room.description: Room where the TV is located

house.tv.<name>.scraper.description:
Scraper tunables applied to every channel on this device.
Any subset may be overridden per channel via
`channels.<name>.scraper`.

house.tv.<name>.scraper.default_duration.description:
Fallback duration when the next entry's start time can't
be parsed.
Scraper default: `30`.

house.tv.<name>.scraper.desc_xpath.description:
XPath relative to a row, locating the description element.
Set to `""` to disable descriptions.
Scraper default: `.//p`.

house.tv.<name>.scraper.pm_heuristic_aft.description:
Only relevant for 12-hour formats that lack an explicit
AM/PM marker. Once the previous programme reached or
passed this hour, later ambiguous AM hours are promoted
to PM. `null` disables the heuristic.
house.tv.<name>.scraper.pm_heuristic_aft.type: null or integer between 0 and 23 (both inclusive)

house.tv.<name>.scraper.row_xpath.description:
XPath selecting each programme row.
Scraper default: `//table[@id="channel-schedule"]//tr`.

house.tv.<name>.scraper.time_attr.description:
Attribute of the time element to read. Set to `""` to
always use the element's text content.
Scraper default: `"datetime"`.

house.tv.<name>.scraper.time_formats.description:
strptime formats tried in order, after ISO 8601 is
attempted.
Scraper default: `[ "%H:%M" "%H.%M" ]`.

house.tv.<name>.scraper.time_strip_patte.description:
Regex applied to the raw time string before strptime.
Set to `""` to disable stripping — required when the
format keeps a literal AM/PM marker.
Scraper default: `"[^\\d:\\.]"`.

house.tv.<name>.scraper.time_xpath.description:
XPath relative to a row, locating the element containing
the start time.
Scraper default: `.//time`.

house.tv.<name>.scraper.timezone_offset_.description:
Fixed offset applied to every parsed time, in hours. May
be fractional (e.g. `5.5`). `null` = use the scraper's
built-in global `TIME_OFFSET`.
house.tv.<name>.scraper.timezone_offset_.type: null or signed integer or floating point number

house.tv.<name>.scraper.title_xpath.description:
XPath relative to a row, locating the title element.
Scraper default: `.//a[contains(@class, "program-title")]`.

house.zigbee.automations.description:
Modular automations for zigduck. Each submodule groups a family of
related event sources:

  mqtt_triggered -> fires when an MQTT topic publishes a matching
                    payload
  time_based     -> fires on a cron expression or structured
                    schedule
  presence_based -> fires after motion has been absent for a
                    configured duration
  greeting       -> fires when the entry door opens after the house
                    has been empty
  dimmer_actions -> per-room overrides for dimmer button events
  room_actions   -> hooks for internal zigduck room events
  global_actions -> hooks for internal zigduck global events

All submodules share the action DSL defined by
`Types.automationActionType`, so any action can be used in any
submodule. Conditions are not shared: `mqtt_triggered` and
`time_based` accept `dark_time | someone_home | room_occupied`,
while `presence_based` accepts `dark_time | room_occupied |
lights_on`.

house.zigbee.automations.dimmer_actions.description:
Per-room overrides for dimmer-switch behaviour. The attribute
name must match a room declared under `house.rooms`. The
reserved key `_default` defines the baseline applied to every
room that does not override a given event; each concrete room
inherits `_default` and may override any subset of the eight
button events.

house.zigbee.automations.dimmer_actions..description:
Override for the down-button hold-and-release event.
`null` uses the built-in default (no action).

Human-readable description of what this handler does.
Shown in generated documentation.

example.text: "Turn off the kitchen fan on hold-release"

house.zigbee.automations.dimmer_actions..description: Whether to enable Enable this dimmer action.

Actions appended after the dimmer's default behaviour.
Use this to add side effects (e.g. switch a fan on)
without replacing the built-in dimming logic.

If non-empty, replaces the default dimmer behaviour
entirely with these actions. Use this to repurpose a
button (e.g. hold "off" to run a scene instead of merely
dimming).

house.zigbee.automations.global_actions.description:
Global automation hooks fired by internal zigduck events that
are not scoped to a room. Key is the event name (e.g.
`leak_detected`, `smoke_detected`, `all_lights_on`,
`security_armed`); value is an ordered action list. String
entries are shorthand for
`{ type = "shell"; command = <string>; }`.
house.zigbee.automations.global_actions.type: attribute set of list of (string or (submodule))

house.zigbee.automations.greeting.description:
The welcome-home automation. Fires `actions` when the
configured door opens after the house has been empty for at
least `awayDuration` seconds.

house.zigbee.automations.greeting.action.description:
Ordered actions executed on arrival. The default is a
shell echo; most users override this with a TTS
command or a notification. String entries are
shorthand for
`{ type = "shell"; command = <string>; }`.

house.zigbee.automations.greeting.awayDu.description:
Minimum seconds the house must have been empty before a
door opening counts as "arriving home". Prevents the
greeting from firing when you just stepped out to take
out the trash.

house.zigbee.automations.greeting.delay.description:
Seconds to wait after the door opens before running
`actions`. Useful when the greeting is TTS that should
play after the door has closed again.

house.zigbee.automations.greeting.door.description:
Friendly name of the door sensor to watch. Required
when `enable = true`; the automation is a no-op when
this is `null`. Must match a `friendly_name` under
`house.zigbee.devices`. Case-sensitive.

house.zigbee.automations.greeting.enable.description: Whether to enable the greeting automation.

house.zigbee.automations.greeting.messag.description:
Field on the door sensor's state payload that flips to
`false` when the door opens. For most Zigbee contact
sensors this is `"contact"`; override only when using
a custom sensor with a different field name.

house.zigbee.automations.mqtt_triggered.description:
Automations driven by incoming MQTT messages. Each attribute
name is the automation's identifier (free-form, shown in
logs). Runs `actions` when `topic` receives a matching
message and every optional `conditions` entry passes.

house.zigbee.automations.mqtt_triggered..description:
Ordered actions executed when `topic` (and `message`,
if set) match and all `conditions` pass. String entries
are shorthand for
`{ type = "shell"; command = <string>; }`.

Conditions that must all pass before `actions` run.
Empty list means the automation fires unconditionally
on a matching message.

Room the condition applies to. Required when
`type = "room_occupied"`; ignored otherwise.

Condition to evaluate before running `actions`:

  dark_time    -> current time is within the dark
                  window configured under
                  `house.zigbee.motion.trigger.lights`
  someone_home -> at least one presence tracker
                  reports home
  room_occupied-> the room named in `room` currently
                  reports occupancy

Expected boolean for the condition. The condition
passes when the computed state equals `value`.
`null` means "any non-empty value".

Human-readable summary shown in logs and generated
documentation. Does not affect behaviour.

example.text: "Toggle living room lights on single button press"

house.zigbee.automations.mqtt_triggered..description: Whether to enable Enable this MQTT-triggered automation.

If set, `actions` fire only when the published payload
equals this string exactly. `null` (the default) fires
on every message published to `topic`, regardless of
payload.

MQTT topic the automation subscribes to. Must be fully
qualified with the broker's `baseTopic` prefix
(default: `zigbee2mqtt/`).

house.zigbee.automations.presence_based.description:
Automations driven by motion absence. Each entry watches
one or more motion sensors and fires `actions` after
`no_motion_duration` seconds of stillness, then optionally
fires `motion_restored_actions` when motion returns.

house.zigbee.automations.presence_based..description:
Ordered actions executed after `no_motion_duration`
seconds without motion, provided every condition
passes. String entries are shorthand for
`{ type = "shell"; command = <string>; }`.

Conditions that must all pass before `actions` run.
`motion_restored_actions` is not gated by these.

Room the condition applies to. Required when
`type` is room-scoped (`room_occupied`); ignored
otherwise.

Condition to evaluate before `actions` run:

  dark_time    -> currently inside the dark window
  room_occupied-> the room currently reports
                  occupancy (useful to suppress
                  auto-off if someone just returned)
  lights_on    -> at least one light in scope is
                  currently on (skips the work
                  when everything is already off)

Expected boolean for the condition. Passes when
the computed state equals `value`.

Human-readable summary shown in logs and generated
documentation. Does not affect behaviour.

example.text: "Turn off kitchen lights after 10 minutes idle"

house.zigbee.automations.presence_based..description: Whether to enable this presence-based automation.

Ordered actions executed when motion is detected again
after `actions` has fired. Use this to restore lighting
without waiting for the normal motion handler to catch
up. Not gated by `conditions`.

Friendly names of the motion sensors to watch. The
automation considers the room idle once every sensor in
this list has reported no motion for
`no_motion_duration` seconds.

Seconds of continuous no-motion before `actions` fire.
A single motion event resets the countdown.

house.zigbee.automations.room_actions.description:
Room-scoped automation hooks fired by internal zigduck
events. Outer key is the room name (must match a room under
`house.rooms`); inner key is the event name emitted by the
room event bus (e.g. `motion_detected`, `motion_not_detected`,
`door_opened`, `door_closed`, `lights_turned_on`); the value
is an ordered action list. String entries are shorthand for
`{ type = "shell"; command = <string>; }`.
house.zigbee.automations.room_actions.type: attribute set of attribute set of list of (string or (submodule))

house.zigbee.automations.time_based.description:
Automations driven by a schedule. `schedule` accepts either a
cron expression or a structured window; see its description
for both forms.

house.zigbee.automations.time_based.<nam.description:
Ordered actions executed when the schedule and every
condition match. String entries are shorthand for
`{ type = "shell"; command = <string>; }`.

Conditions that must all pass at fire time. Empty list
means the automation fires unconditionally.

Room the condition applies to. Required when
`type = "room_occupied"`; ignored otherwise.

Same condition vocabulary as `mqtt_triggered`:

  dark_time    -> currently inside the dark window
  someone_home -> at least one presence tracker home
  room_occupied-> the room named in `room` reports
                  occupancy

Expected boolean for the condition. Passes when
the computed state equals `value`.

Human-readable summary shown in logs and generated
documentation. Does not affect behaviour.
Whether to enable this time-based automation.

When the automation fires. Either:

  string-> a standard 5-field cron expression
           (e.g. `"0 22 * * *"` = every day at 22:00)

  attrset-> structured `{ start; end; days; }` for the
            common "within this window" case

house.zigbee.coordinator.description: Serial port device mapping by USB IDs

house.zigbee.coordinator.adapter.description:
Zigbee2MQTT adapter type used to communicate with the coordinator.

For Zigbee2MQTT 2.x and newer, this should normally be set to
the adapter type expected by your coordinator. Common values
include "zstack" for Texas Instruments coordinators.

If you are unsure, leave the default value unchanged.

house.zigbee.coordinator.productId.description:
USB product ID of the Zigbee coordinator, in hexadecimal.

You can find this with `lsusb`. For example, if it reports
`ID 10c3:ea61`, the product ID is `ea61`.

Together with `vendorId`, this identifies the coordinator USB
device.

house.zigbee.coordinator.symlink.description:
Name of the stable symlink to create under /dev.

For example, setting this to "zigbee" creates /dev/zigbee,
which can then be used as the serial device for Zigbee2MQTT.

Using a symlink avoids depending on unstable device names such
as /dev/ttyUSB0, which can change when USB devices are plugged
in or removed.

house.zigbee.coordinator.vendorId.description:
USB vendor ID of the Zigbee coordinator, in hexadecimal.

You can find this with `lsusb`. For example, if it reports
`ID 10c3:ea61`, the vendor ID is `10c3`.

This is used together with `productId` to identify the correct
USB device, regardless of which /dev/ttyUSB* or /dev/ttyACM*
device name Linux assigns to it.

house.zigbee.dataDir.description:
Directory where Zigbee2MQTT stores its persistent state
(paired-device database, coordinator backup, logs, …).
The service creates and owns this directory at runtime;
it is **not** part of the Nix store.

house.zigbee.devices.description: Zigbee device definitions keyed by device ID.

house.zigbee.devices.<name>.batteryType.description: Optional type of battery the device uses.

house.zigbee.devices.<name>.endpoint.description: The Zigbee endpoint to control this device.

house.zigbee.devices.<name>.hue_id.description: The light_id for the device (Hue integration).

house.zigbee.devices.<name>.icon.description: Material Design icon name representing this device.

house.zigbee.devices.<name>.room.description: The room this device belongs to.

house.zigbee.dimmer.description: Configuration for dimmer switches. Default configuration is for the Philips Hue Dimmer Switch. You can check the message for your specific dimmer at zigbee2MQTT documentation.

house.zigbee.dimmer.actions.downPress.description: Action for single press of DOWN button

house.zigbee.dimmer.actions.offPress.description: Action for single press of OFF button

house.zigbee.dimmer.actions.onPress.description: Action for single press of ON button

house.zigbee.dimmer.actions.upPress.description: Action for single press of UP button

house.zigbee.dimmer.doubleClickTimeout.description: Timeout for double-click detection in milliseconds. Double clicking will result in scene cycle on the lights in the dimmer's defined room.

house.zigbee.dimmer.message.description: MQTT field name containing dimmer action

house.zigbee.hueSyncBox.description: Philips Hue Bridge & Sync Box configuration for TV to lights syncing

house.zigbee.hueSyncBox.bridge.ip.description: IP address of the Philips Hue Bridge

house.zigbee.hueSyncBox.bridge.passwordF.description:
Path to a file containing the Hue Bridge API key (username).
To get a key, press the physical button on your Hue Bridge, then run:
  curl -X POST http://<bridge-ip>/api -d '{"devicetype":"house#nixos"}'
The response will contain a `username` field – save that string in this file.

house.zigbee.hueSyncBox.enable.description: Whether to enable Enable Philips Hue Bridge & Sync Box integration.

house.zigbee.hueSyncBox.syncBox.ip.description: IP address of the Philips Hue Sync Box

house.zigbee.hueSyncBox.syncBox.password.description:
Path to a file containing the Hue Sync Box API token.
To get a token, run the following command:
  curl -k -sS -X POST "https://<SYNC_BOX_IP>/api/v1/registrations" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"appName": "zigduck", "instanceName": "zigduck"}'
Then press and hold the physical button on the Sync Box until the LED turns green, then send the command again.
The response will contain the API token.

house.zigbee.hueSyncBox.syncBox.tv.description: What TV should syncBox synchronize the lights to. Available TVs: shield

house.zigbee.mosquitto.description:
MQTT broker (Mosquitto) connection used by the Zigbee stack:
host, credentials, base topic, optional field whitelist, and
TLS client certificates. Set to `null` to disable MQTT integration.

house.zigbee.mosquitto.baseTopic.description: MQTT base topic used by Zigbee2mqtt and the zigduck runtime.

house.zigbee.mosquitto.host.description: IP address of the host running Mosquitto

house.zigbee.mosquitto.passwordFile.description: Path to file containing MQTT password

house.zigbee.mosquitto.ssl.description: TLS settings for the MQTT connection. Enable this when the broker requires client-certificate authentication.

house.zigbee.mosquitto.ssl.clientKeyFile.description: Path to client private key file

house.zigbee.mosquitto.ssl.enable.description: Whether to enable Enable SSL/TLS for MQTT connection.

house.zigbee.mosquitto.whitelist.description: Optional list of additional JSON fields to include in states.json

house.zigbee.motion.description:
Motion-detection settings shared by all Zigbee motion sensors:
whether handling is enabled at all, whether it only fires when
it is dark, and what to trigger (e.g. turning lights on).

house.zigbee.motion.enable.description: Whether to enable Enable Zigbee motion handling.

house.zigbee.motion.trigger.description:
What to do when motion is detected. Currently this covers
turning a set of Zigbee lights on for a configurable
duration, within an optional hour-of-day window.

house.zigbee.motion.trigger.lights.after.description: Lights activate only after this hour (24h)

house.zigbee.motion.trigger.lights.befor.description: Lights activate only before this hour (24h)

house.zigbee.motion.trigger.lights.durat.description: Seconds to keep lights on after motion

house.zigbee.motion.trigger.lights.trans.description:
Whether to fade the lights out over `duration`
rather than keeping them at full brightness and
then switching off at the end of `duration`.

house.zigbee.motion.when.dark.enable.description: Whether to enable only react to motion while it is dark (i.e. between sunset and sunrise, or per the light-level sensor).

house.zigbee.networkKeyFile.description:
Path to a file containing the Zigbee network key used by
Zigbee2MQTT (`network_key`). The path is read at **runtime**
by the service; the contents are never copied into the Nix
store.

The network key identifies and secures the Zigbee network. Keep
this key stable: changing or losing it will require Zigbee
devices to be paired with the network again.

The file should contain the key in the following format:

```yaml
- 86
- 208
- ...
```

house.zigbee.no.motion.description:
Settings for the "no motion" automation: what to do when no
motion has been detected for a while (typically: turn selected
Zigbee lights off).

house.zigbee.no.motion.trigger.all.description:
"No motion" automation applied to *all* Zigbee lights:
once motion has cleared (see `after`), turn the listed
lights off, except those in `exclude` which keep their
current state (e.g. night lights).

house.zigbee.no.motion.trigger.all.light.description: Turn off all Zigbee lights after motion has cleared.

Time in minutes after the last detected motion
before all (non-excluded) lights are turned off.
Whether to enable the no-motion lights-off automation (turn lights off once motion clears).

Device names (keys under `house.zigbee.devices`)
to skip when turning lights off; they keep their
current state.

house.zigbee.scenes.type: attribute set of attribute set of (attribute set)

house.zigbee.settings.description:
Please note that this flake already handles the configuration of Zigbee2MQTT internally.
These would be overrides.
Your configuration.yaml as a Nix attribute set.
Check the [documentation](https://www.zigbee2mqtt.io/information/configuration.html) for possible options.
